pageCache.text:
Fulfilment, Belonging, Independence
Privileged to work with young people whose courage and talents help them to overcome some very significant challenges on their journey to adulthood.
Privileged too, working with colleagues who respond to each young person as an individual, always striving for the best possible outcomes and taking learning from every issue that arises.
We believe Ickburgh School is a place where pupils can find Fulfilment, Belonging and greater Independence. We serve young people aged from 3 to 19 with severe learning difficulties, severe learning difficulties and autism, and profound and multiple learning difficulties.
We look forward to hearing from you

pageCache.text:
Music, Art, and Performing Arts
Curriculum
Here at Ickburgh School we love Music and Performing Arts. We believe it enriches our students' lives and provides vital opportunities for expression and communication.
You can find below our Music, Art, and Performing Arts Strategy document.
Our students perform at a range of different community events, including the 'Shakespeare in Schools' festival where students perform on a professional stage, and the Hackney Music and Dance Festivals. We've also enjoyed very successful partnerships with Sadlers Wells, the London Symphony Orchestra, and The Yard Theatre, enjoying and participating in performances. In recognition of our excellence, we are a Music Mark School: https://www.musicmark.org.uk/join/schools/

Challenge Partners
Our School
Challenge Partners is an education charity, led by practitioners, through which schools collaborate to improve each other and the education system as a whole, so all children benefit.
They work with schools across the country, and focus on school improvement, leadership development and knowledge exchange. Their programmes are grounded in evidence of what works, regular quality assurance, and sharing the collective wisdom in our schools.
The school has an regular review, led by senior leaders from other special schools. Below is our most recent report.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ickburgh School - Support with strategies for parents/carers
pageCache.text:
Support with strategies for parents/carers
Learning at Home
Approach or Strategy
https://classroom.thenational.academy/lessons/sensory-stories-74vpar?activity=video&step=1&view=1
Sensory stories tell a story using words and sensory stimuli. Usually there are just a few sentences in a sensory story (10 or less) and each sentence is paired with a sensory stimulus. The sensory stimuli don't just support the words in telling the story, if well chosen, they tell the story in their own right. Sensory stories can help young people to develop their communication and understanding.
All pupils, especially Sensory Learners
https://classroom.thenational.academy/lessons/building-simple-sentences-6cvkcd?activity=video&step=1
Colourful semantics is a targeted approach to support children with their sentence building and to teach them about sentence structure.
Active and Connecting Learners
Observe Wait Listen (OWL)
https://classroom.thenational.academy/lessons/early-attention-6gv6ad?activity=video&step=1
OWLing is all about being a good communication partner. While OWL stands for three separate skills (observing, waiting, and listening), a good communication partner really needs to be doing all three at once.
